Subject: Springboard renewal — capacity growth plan & GPU recommendation

Hi Ellie and David,

Thanks for the conversation last week. As you start the renewal window, I wanted to share a concise capacity plan that lines up with the traffic growth you described (higher QPS and longer context for a subset of inference jobs). Attached is a short forecast (springboard-qps-forecast.xlsx) and an updated Dedicated term offer (redwood-dedicated-offer-v3.pdf).

Top-level recommendation: add a 12-GPU reserved pool (NVIDIA A100-class equivalent) to your existing Dedicated commitment and convert 20% of burst traffic to the reserved pool for predictable throughput. That maps to ~18% latency improvement for the 4k-context generation path in our perf runs and gives room for the 40% projected QPS increase in Q3.

Next steps I propose:
- Ellie: confirm whether procurement wants a single annual renewal or a 24-month term with quarterly commit reviews.
- David: can you share any specific 95th-percentile latency targets we should bake into the SLA?
- Marissa / Karthik: please review the attached GPU-sizing notes and call out any operational constraints (autoscaling guardrails, preemption windows).

I'll follow up with a short runbook and a timeline for the rollover.

Best,
Rachel

Thanks Rachel — received, and I skimmed the forecast. High level thoughts:
- We are likely to move to a 24-month term (budget cycles) but need a FY27 cap on monthly spend from procurement.
- Our product team is targeting a 35–45% QPS increase in the model-serving tier in Q3; the heavier prompt paths (longer context + retrieval) are the main driver.
- 95th-percentile latency target: keep < 350ms for the short path (512 tokens) and < 1.2s for the 4k path.

Can Marissa confirm whether the 12-GPU reserved pool assumes homogeneous instance type and whether we can mix quantized variants to reduce cost?

Ellie

Ellie — quick answers from infra sizing:
- The 12-GPU pool we suggested is modeled as 12x L40s for predictable throughput in our benchmarks. You can mix in 4x quantized VMs to serve low-cost embed/rerank traffic, but the primary generation path should be homogeneous to keep latency stable under batching.
- If you shift ~25% of traffic to quantized variants, the effective cost drops ~18% while preserving p50 latency; p95 for long-context generations is slightly worse (~5–8% increase).
- For the SLA numbers you gave (350ms / 1.2s), keeping a 20% headroom buffer in the reserved pool is prudent. That means the 12-GPU pool should be sized for current baseline + 45% growth, not just the mean forecast.

I'll attach a short runbook with autoscaling thresholds and cache-warmup steps in my next note.

Marissa

Appreciate the clarity. A few procurement/ops questions before we loop legal:
1) Can Redwood provide an explicit throughput SLA (tokens/sec) tied to the reserved pool and define fallback policy if we exceed the pool (e.g., soft throttling, overflow to burst at X% cost uplift)?
2) Do you offer a committed burst credit that we can buy to smooth seasonal peaks?

Also, attached is a short internal spec (not attached here) showing peak day patterns for Q2. If you can map the SLA language to the pricing PDF we can align on the redlines.

Thanks,
David

Hi David / Ellie — following up with concrete answers to the two asks; summarizing so procurement has language to take to legal.

1) Throughput SLA and overflow policy (proposal):
- SLA: reserved pool capacity guaranteed to sustain 8M tokens/min aggregate (measured at request ingress) for the 12-GPU pool with p95 latency targets of < 1.2s on the 4k path.
- Overflow policy: when reserved pool capacity is saturated, traffic will automatically spill to your burst tier at a configurable uplift. Default uplift: +60% per-token cost for overflow traffic; customer can set a hard cap to reject overflow at X% above quota.

2) Committed burst credit: we offer a pre-purchased burst credit pack (1M tokens/month blocks) that applies before pay-as-you-go burst billing. Packs are discounted at 12% vs on-demand burst pricing and can be sized per quarter.

Operational notes: we will provide an SLA appendix that ties these guarantees to monitoring hooks in the Redwood Console (per-route token counters, p95 tracing) and automated rollback if performance regressions are detected on new model variants.

If that looks good, Rachel — can you add a one-line term change (24-month term with quarterly capacity review) to the quote and re-issue the PDF? We will also include the committed burst pack as an optional line item.

Thanks — Karthik
